arxiv-1912-04915.title: Strain induced superconductor-insulator transition on Lieb lattice
arxiv-1912-04915.creator: Nyayabanta Swain, Madhuparna Karmakar
arxiv-1912-04915.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Nyayabanta Swain, Madhuparna Karmakar. We report the numerical investigation of strain induced superconductor-insulator quantum phase transition on a Lieb lattice. Based on a non perturbative Monte Carlo technique, which retains the spatial fluctuations of the superconducting pairing field at all orders but neglects the temporal fluctuations, we show that in two dimensions an s s -wave superconductor undergoes transition to a highly correlated bosonic insulator under the influence of strain, applied as staggered hopping amplitudes.

arxiv-2301-01425.title: Renormalizing Antiferroelectric Nanostripes in β ′ − In 2 ​ Se 3 \beta^{\prime}-\rm{In}_{2}\rm{Se}_{3} via Optomechanics
arxiv-2301-01425.creator: Zihang Wu, Kun Liu, Xingchi Mu, Jian Zhou
arxiv-2301-01425.description: Abstract Antiferroelectric (AFE) materials have received tremendous attention owing to their high energy conversion efficiency and good tunability. Recently, an exotic two-dimensional (2D) AFE material, β ′ − In 2 ​ Se 3 \beta^{\prime}-\rm In_{2}Se_{3} monolayer that could host atomically thin AFE nanostripe domains has been experimentally synthesized and theoretically examined.

arxiv-2403-19973.title: FaiRTT: An Empirical Approach for Enhanced RTT Fairness and Bottleneck Throughput in BBR
arxiv-2403-19973.creator: Akshita Abrol 1 , Purnima Murali Mohan 1 , Tram Truong-Huu 1 2
arxiv-2403-19973.description: Abstract In next-generation networks, achieving Round-trip Time (RTT) fairness is essential for ensuring fair bandwidth distribution among diverse flow types, enhancing overall network utilization. The TCP congestion control algorithm — BBR, was proposed by Google to dynamically adjust sending rates in response to changing network conditions.

arxiv-2411-15338.title: On Computational Completeness of Semi-Conditional Matrix Grammars
arxiv-2411-15338.creator: Henning Fernau, Lakshmanan Kuppusamy, Indhumathi Raman
arxiv-2411-15338.description: Abstract Matrix grammars are one of the first approaches ever proposed in regulated rewriting, prescribing that rules have to be applied in a certain order. Originally, they have been introduced by Ábrahám on linguistic grounds. In traditional regulated rewriting, the most interesting case shows up when all rules are context-free.

arxiv-2505-06646.title: Reproducing and Improving CheXNet: Deep Learning for Chest X-ray Disease Classification
arxiv-2505-06646.creator: Daniel Strick, Carlos Garcia, Anthony Huang
arxiv-2505-06646.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel Strick, Carlos Garcia, Anthony Huang. Deep learning for radiologic image analysis is a rapidly growing field in biomedical research and is likely to become a standard practice in modern medicine. On the publicly available NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset (also hosted on Kaggle), containing X-ray images that are classified by the presence or absence of 14 different diseases, we reproduced an algorithm known as CheXNet, as well as explored other algorithms that outperform CheXNet’s baseline metrics.

arxiv-2509-15772.title: Vision–Language Models as Differentiable Semantic and Spatial Rewards for Text-to-3D Generation
arxiv-2509-15772.creator: Weimin Bai, Yubo Li, Weijian Luo, Wenzheng Chen, He Sun[2pt] 1. Peking University2. Xiaohongshu Inc[2pt] weiminbai@stu.pku.edu.cn; hesun@pku.edu.cn [4pt] Project page: https://ai4scientificimaging.org/vlm3d
arxiv-2509-15772.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Weimin Bai, Yubo Li, Weijian Luo, Wenzheng Chen, He Sun[2pt] 1. Peking University2. Xiaohongshu Inc[2pt] weiminbai@stu.pku.edu.cn; hesun@pku.edu.cn [4pt] Project page: https://ai4scientificimaging.org/vlm3d. Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) enables high-quality text-to-3D generation by supervising 3D models through the denoising of multi-view 2D renderings, using a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model to align with the input prompt and ensure 3D consistency.

arxiv-2510-13817.title: Large Language Models for Real - World IoT Device Identification Conference: ; ; CCS: Security and privacy Mobile and wireless security CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in ubiquitous and mobile computing
arxiv-2510-13817.creator: Rameen Mahmood, Tousif Ahmed, Sai Teja Peddinti, Danny Yuxing Huang
arxiv-2510-13817.description: Abstract . The rapid expansion of IoT devices has outpaced current identification methods, creating significant risks for security, privacy, and network accountability. These challenges are heightened in open - world environments, where traffic metadata is often incomplete, noisy, or intentionally obfuscated. We introduce a semantic inference pipeline that reframes device identification as a language modeling task over heterogeneous network metadata.

arxiv-2601-00272.title: Efficient Algorithms for Adversarially Robust Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
arxiv-2601-00272.creator: Alexandr Andoni, Themistoklis Haris, Esty Kelman, Krzysztof Onak
arxiv-2601-00272.description: Abstract We study the Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) problem under a powerful adaptive adversary that controls both the dataset and a sequence of Q Q queries. Primarily, for the high-dimensional regime of d = ω ⁡ ( Q ) d=\omega(\sqrt{Q}) , we introduce a sequence of algorithms with progressively stronger guarantees.

arxiv-2602-16386.title: Towards Secure and Interoperable Data Spaces for 6G: The 6G-DALI Approach Thanks: This work has received funding from the Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking (SNS JU) under the European Union’s Horizon Europe Research and Innovation programme under Grant Agreement No 101192750.
arxiv-2602-16386.creator: Dimitrios Amaxilatis, Themistoklis Sarantakos, Nikolaos Tsironis, Vasileios Theodorou, Christos Verikoukis
arxiv-2602-16386.description: Abstract The next generation of mobile networks, 6G, is expected to enable data-driven services at unprecedented scale and complexity, with stringent requirements for trust, interoperability, and automation. Central to this vision is the ability to create, manage, and share high-quality datasets across distributed and heterogeneous environments.

pmc-10571953.title: Does Vaccine-Induced Maternally-Derived Immunity Protect Swine Offspring against Influenza a Viruses? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Challenge Trials from 1990 to May 2021
pmc-10571953.creator: Sheila Keay, Zvonimir Poljak, Famke Alberts, Annette O’Connor, Robert Friendship, Terri L O’Sullivan, Jan M Sargeant, Silvan Urfer, Sebastian Patrick Arlt, David Ramey
pmc-10571953.description: Simple SummaryVaccinated mother pigs can pass vaccine protection (immunity) onto their offspring, but in the case of influenza, the benefit is not clear. Influenza viruses evolve rapidly and can sometimes change their appearance to the point of becoming a new stain that evades a pig’s immune defenses.

pmc-10648992.title: LRRK2 Attenuates Antioxidant Response in Familial Parkinson’s Disease Derived Neural Stem Cells
pmc-10648992.creator: Jeffrey Kim, Etienne W. Daadi, Elyas Sebastien Daadi, Thomas Oh, Michela Deleidi, Marcel M. Daadi
pmc-10648992.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disease, characterized by the loss of midbrain dopaminergic neurons which leads to impaired motor and cognitive functions. PD is predominantly an idiopathic disease; however, about 5% of cases are linked to hereditary mutations.

pmc-10735490.title: INEQUALITIES IN OLD AGE WELL-BEING: THE ROLE OF REGIONAL DEPOPULATION AND SOCIAL AND MATERIAL CONDITIONS
pmc-10735490.creator: Martina Brandt, Alina Schmitz
pmc-10735490.description: Material conditions and social integration are important predictors of wellbeing in old age. It can be expected that older individuals who reside in depopulating areas experience declines in well-being, as their property loses value, their social networks are shrinking, and public infrastructure is lacking.

pmc-11561210.title: 12-Month Time in Tight Range Improvement with Advanced Hybrid-Closed Loop System in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes
pmc-11561210.creator: Laura Nigi, Maria De Los Angeles Simon Batzibal, Dorica Cataldo, Francesco Dotta
pmc-11561210.description: IntroductionTime in tight range (TITR) is an emerging and valuable metric for assessing normoglycemia. The latest advancement in automated insulin delivery (AID) systems, the advanced hybrid closed-loop (AHCL) systems, are particularly noteworthy for managing type 1 diabetes (T1D) and enhancing glycemic control.

pmc-12843287.title: Improving Prognostic Stratification in Gastric Cancer: The Role of Lymph Node Staging Systems
pmc-12843287.creator: Tudor Razvan Grigorie, Cosmin Verdea, Teodora Delia Chiriac, Iulia Magdalena Gramaticu, Andreea Iliesiu, George Andrei Popescu, Mihai Popescu, Sorin Tiberiu Alexandrescu
pmc-12843287.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: The tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) classification system is the standard for staging gastric cancer and predicting survival. However, its accuracy can be compromised by insufficient lymph node (LN) dissection during surgery or inadequate pathologic examination. Alternative staging systems, such as the lymph node ratio (LNR) and log odds of positive lymph nodes (LODDS), may provide better prognostic value when LN examination is suboptimal.

pmc-13068506.title: Digital Strategies Utilised to Encourage Undergraduate Nursing Students' Engagement in Online Units of Study Throughout the COVID‐19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review
pmc-13068506.creator: Chanchal Kurup, Abigail Ford, Penny Heidke
pmc-13068506.description: AimThis systematic review provides an overview of digital strategies utilised to encourage undergraduate nursing students' engagement in online units of study throughout the COVID‐19 pandemic.BackgroundIn nursing education, engagement was crucial in acquiring knowledge, skills, critical thinking and problem‐solving abilities. The COVID‐19 pandemic forced schools and universities worldwide to quickly adapt from face‐to‐face learning to online platforms.

pmc-13159358.title: The anesthesiologist’s perspective in choosing between robotic-assisted and conventional laparoscopic urological surgery: a propensity score-matched analysis
pmc-13159358.creator: Meiyu Wei, Ce Zhang, Dongnan Hou, Lijie Wen, Bo Yang
pmc-13159358.description: BackgroundComparative studies between robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgery (RALS) and conventional laparoscopic surgery (CLS) primarily focus on surgical outcomes, with limited emphasis on the anesthesiologist's perspective. This study aimed to compare anesthesia-related Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) outcomes to inform surgical decision-making.

pmc-13277126.title: A tRNA-derived fragment tRF3019a promotes LUAD metastasis by stabilizing hnRNPK and enhancing MYH11 expression
pmc-13277126.creator: Xin Li, Weifang Cui, Zhangjie Wang, Danyao Chen, Zhenyu Kuang, Junjie Jiang, Yuwei Lai, Xiongzhou Zhang, Chaojun Duan, Chunfang Zhang, Xizhe Li
pmc-13277126.description: BackgroundtRNA-derived fragments (tRFs) have been shown to play important regulatory roles in cancer biology. However, the impact of tRFs on lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains largely unexplored.MethodsThe differential expression of tRF3019a, a tRNA fragment derived from tRNA-Ala (AGC), was identified through database mining and subsequently validated by quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT–PCR) in pathological tissues obtained from 100 patients with LUAD.

pmc-13528761.title: Duty to Protect? The Troubling Pattern of Legislative Noncompliance and Missed Police Involvement in Ontario’s Long-Term Care Sector
pmc-13528761.creator: Vivian Stamatopoulos, Shannon Vettor, Emily Hladkowicz
pmc-13528761.description: BackgroundOntario’s Fixing Long-Term Care Act, 2021 requires long-term care (LTC) licensees to immediately notify police of any alleged, suspected, or witnessed abuse, neglect, or other conduct that may constitute a criminal offence. This study examines compliance with mandatory police notification requirements using publicly available Ministry of Long-Term Care (MLTC) inspection reports.

pmc-13556896.title: 481. Effects of palmitoylethanolamide on psychic distress and daily functioning in autistic adults: a nonrandomized open-label trial
pmc-13556896.creator: R Bortoletto, M Garzitto, M Basaldella, C Scipioni, O Sepulcri, M Fabris, F Curcio, M Colizzi
pmc-13556896.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAutistic adults lack treatments for co-occurring psychic distress and mental health challenges. pmc-13676994.title: H‐Bonding‐Induced Repulsion Between Small Groups Toward a Highly Puckered Benzene
pmc-13676994.creator: Chaofeng Zhao, Qi Sun, Ning Ding, Xiaoting Ren, Jinxuan He, Shenghua Li, Siping Pang
pmc-13676994.description: Benzene ring puckering generally arises from the strong repulsion between bulky substituents, while in this study, we present that benzene ring puckering can be achieved by repulsion between small substituents (nitro and methyl groups) facilitated by hydrogen‐bonding attraction, as exemplified in 1,3,5‐trinitro‐2,4,6‐trimethylaminobenzene.

pmc-13687969.title: Novel method for displaying the contact index in fixed-loop pulsed field ablation catheters
pmc-13687969.creator: Kazuki Ito, Yoshihisa Naruse, Makoto Sano, Yuichiro Maekawa
pmc-13687969.description: ovel jumper-cable modification overcomes native system constraints by duplicating and rerouting electrode signals on the 3-dimensional mapping platform. This approach enables complete real-time visualization of contact index across all 9 electrodes of a fixed-loop pulsed field ablation catheter.•Impedance-based contact index feedback provides objective, electrode-specific confirmation of tissue contact before pulse delivery.

uslaw-usc-t10-s7443.title: 10 U.S.C. § 7443 — Cadets: appointment; to bring Corps to full strength
uslaw-usc-t10-s7443.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7443.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part III (Training); Chapter 753 (United States Military Academy). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. If it is determined that, upon the admission of a new class to the Academy, the number of cadets at the Academy will be below the authorized number, the Secretary of the Army may fill the vacancies by nominating additional cadets.
